changeJustifications.summary: Added the pure `derive_include_roots(&[String]) -> Vec<String>` (every proper directory prefix whose last segment is exactly `include`/`inc`, case-sensitive lower, sorted+deduped via BTreeSet — deterministic for any file order); replaced `IncludeResolverConfig.conventional_roots: Vec<&'static str>` with `derived_roots: Vec<String>` and had `build_include_resolution_map` derive them from the indexed file list and pool them with configured roots (resolution order and pooling-to-ambiguity unchanged). Added a `resolver_for(paths)` test helper, moved the 19 pre-existing unit tests onto the derived path (names+assertions unchanged), added the 9 `derived_root*` tests (one per §2.2 taxonomy row), and renamed `configured_root_wins_over_conventional` → `configured_and_conventional_both_matching_is_ambiguous` (body unchanged, per D-TME-TEST-NAME-1). This is the fix at the cause for RC-10: per-module `include/` roots now resolve.

The one construction site now passes only the configured (`--include-root`) roots and `derived_roots: Vec::new()`; the three repo-root-anchored literals `include`/`inc`/`src/include` are removed — they are subsumed by the derived roots (the root-level case). Deriving inside `build_include_resolution_map` is what lets this site pass no conventional list.

`MODULES_LIST_UNRESOLVED_IMPORT_CATEGORIES` gains `ImportsAmbiguousMatch` (now the full four-category IMPORTS family) so the modules-list headline counts include-root-overlap ambiguity where the user reads the unresolved-import count; the doc comment no longer claims the exclusion. The unit test `is_imports_category_only_matches_imports_file_not_found` (a misnomer — it never asserted 'only') is expanded to assert all four import categories and rejects others, and renamed `is_imports_category_accepts_all_four_import_categories_and_rejects_others`.

The modules-list unresolved-count regression test is renamed `modules_list_unresolved_import_count_includes_all_import_categories` and now inserts an `imports_ambiguous_match` edge among the four counted import categories plus one CALLS edge, asserting the total is 4 (ambiguity counted, calls excluded) — pinning that the shared category set stays the full IMPORTS family.

New source→store end-to-end test (CIR-C05): writes a C++ include fixture, indexes it through cpp-extractor+indexer+storage, and asserts (a) a header under a per-module `include/` root resolves to exactly one FILE→FILE IMPORTS edge with no imports_file_not_found row, and (b) the same header under two per-module roots yields no resolved edge and exactly one counted `imports_ambiguous_match` row — never a silent pick.

limitations: gstreamer's second cause (meson subprojects / gst-libs headers never under an `include`/`inc` directory) is out of scope — it is CPP-INCLUDE-ROOTS-2 (RG-REQ-006-L11, the unique multi-segment suffix fallback, ratified 2026-09-14 as its own slice). Root-name matching is case-sensitive lower-case only (`Include`/`INC` derive nothing) — a stated, counted conservatism, proven by the unit test `derived_root_is_case_sensitive`, not a guess.
